name: open-sp
why: An SGML parser from the openjade lineage, a window into the pre-XML markup world that most developers have never touched.

brief.what_it_is: OpenSP is the SGML/XML parsing part of the OpenJade project's SP suite. The homepage describes OpenJade as maintaining Jade, James Clark's DSSSL implementation, and 'the related SP suite of SGML/XML processing tools.' The homepage does not describe the individual tools. The brew metadata lists six executables (onsgmls, osgmlnorm, ospam, ospcat, ospent, osx) and the description 'SGML parser', but the page does not say what each one reads or writes. The page's only stated version for OpenSP is 1.5.1 as the latest stable release.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames the project as a community effort by the DSSSL community to maintain and extend Jade and the related SP tools. It does not give a separate motivation for OpenSP.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the brew formula name is on the homepage. The page links to download and documentation pages but gives no build or setup steps in the text I received. The page does not mention a runtime, accounts, or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: The brew metadata's scout note calls it a window into the pre-XML SGML world. That fits the homepage, which frames SGML as the older standard that both Jade and SP handle, with XML as a secondary target. The DSSSL lineage (a stylesheet language for formatting SGML) is the unusual part of the family.
brief.status: Unknown. The page names OpenSP 1.5.1 as the latest stable release and OpenJade 1.3.2 as the latest stable, with a 1.4devel development release. It gives no release dates. It mentions CVS and SVN repositories and SourceForge hosting, which suggests the project's infrastructure dates from the SourceForge era. I did not find a dated release or recent commit to confirm activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage is the OpenJade distribution page, not an OpenSP page, so it describes the wider project more than this formula. It does not name the license, only saying OpenJade and OpenSP are 'distributed under the same license as Jade', and it does not name that license. The brew formula's executables are not described anywhere on the page. I did not follow the documentation links because the page text did not include their URLs, so the command reference is unverified.
quotes: Jade is James Clark's implementation of DSSSL -- Document Style Semantics and Specification Language -- an ISO standard for formatting SGML (and XML) documents.
OpenJade is a project undertaken by the DSSSL community to maintain and extend Jade, as well as the related SP suite of SGML/XML processing tools.
The latest stable release of OpenSP is 1.5.1.
fetch_log: https://openjade.sourceforge.net/ — fetched, worked; OpenJade distribution page with version info and links, no OpenSP command documentation in the text. No further fetches: the page text did not give URLs for the OpenSP documentation or download pages.

judge.reason: OpenSP’s SGML parsing, validation, and conversion tools offer a hands-on way to explore a richer, mostly forgotten markup standard beyond XML.

entry.title: OpenSP
entry.tldr: OpenSP is James Clark's SGML parser suite, the old pre-XML markup toolkit, installed as onsgmls, osx and a few other small tools.
entry.deeper_look:
OpenSP is the parsing half of the OpenJade project. The homepage describes OpenJade as a community effort to maintain Jade, James Clark's implementation of DSSSL, "as well as the related SP suite of SGML/XML processing tools." OpenSP is that SP suite. The page names 1.5.1 as the latest stable release.

SGML is the standard generalized markup language, the older and far more elaborate ancestor of XML and HTML. DSSSL, the Document Style Semantics and Specification Language, is an ISO standard for formatting SGML and XML documents. The homepage calls it a stylesheet language for that purpose. Jade implements it, and SP does the parsing underneath.

The formula installs six executables: onsgmls, osgmlnorm, ospam, ospcat, ospent and osx. The homepage does not say what each one reads or writes, so this entry does not guess beyond the names. The name onsgmls suggests a parser that checks and reports on SGML documents, and osx suggests conversion to XML, but those are inferences. The --help output is the place to confirm.

The door here is history. Before XML simplified things, SGML was how serious documentation was marked up, and many of XML's rules exist as reactions to it. Running a real SGML parser shows what was cut and why.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the usage and options of the SGML parser, the best starting point for learning what it accepts.
Prints the usage of the osx tool, so you can see what it reads and writes.
Prints the usage of ospcat, another tool in the suite.

entry.whats_unique: It is a working parser from the original SGML and DSSSL era, written by the person behind Jade. Few current tools let you run real SGML rather than XML.
entry.caveats: The homepage is the OpenJade page rather than an OpenSP one, gives no release dates, and does not document the individual commands, so expect to learn them from the help output.
